title: Cohen structure theorem: a complete local ring is a quotient of a power series ring over a field or a Cohen ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring (a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated (for instance $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) and which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $p\ge0$ be the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. Then there exist an integer $n\ge0$, a ring $\Lambda$ which is a field of characteristic $0$ if $p=0$ and a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] with residue characteristic $p$ if $p>0$, and a surjective ring homomorphism $\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to R$ from the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), part (2), and the last paragraph of its proof (the map Lambda[[x_1..x_n]] -> R, x_i -> y_i for generators y_i of m, surjective by Lemma 0315 lemma-completion-generalities). The theorem says 'Lambda is either a field or a Cohen ring'; that Lambda is a field of characteristic 0 when p = 0 (a coefficient field, isomorphic to kappa) and a Cohen ring when p > 0 is the case distinction of the proof (paragraphs 1 and 2: Cohen ring from Lemma 0328 cohen-rings-exist). Part (1) is the existing node lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists.

proof.text: Use Submodule.fg_iff_exists_fin_generating_family to choose n and y:Fin n -> R spanning m. Every y_i belongs to m by subset_span. This includes n=0 when m=0. Completeness of R supplies Hausdorffness for m.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A(2), proof: first and second paragraphs and the last paragraph; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A.

proof.text: If p=0, take Lambda=ResidueField R. CharP.charP_to_charZero gives characteristic zero and Field.toIsField gives IsField. Apply exists_residue_section to get alpha:Lambda -> R with residue composed with alpha equal to the identity; hence that composite is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A(2), proof: first and second paragraphs and the last paragraph; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A.

proof.text: If p is prime, exists_cohenRing supplies Lambda, IsCohenRing p Lambda, and e:Lambda/(p) ≃+* ResidueField R. Apply exists_cohenRing_lift to obtain alpha:Lambda -> R with residue composed with alpha equal to e composed with the quotient map. Both factors are surjective, so the composite is surjective. This packages the compatible lifts and inverse limit of the original steps 3-4. CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero covers the two cases; primality implies p is nonzero.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A(2), proof: first and second paragraphs and the last paragraph; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A.

proof.text: For either coefficient map alpha with surjective residue composite, apply MvPowerSeries.exists_ringHom_of_isAdicComplete to m, alpha, and y. It gives phi:Lambda[[X_1,...,X_n]] -> R with phi(C a)=alpha(a) and phi(X_i)=y_i.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A(2), proof: first and second paragraphs and the last paragraph; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A.

proof.text: Let I=span(range X). By the Mathlib power-series completeness instance the source is I-adically complete. Ideal.map_span and the variable-value equality give I.map phi=span(range y)=m. Therefore R is Hausdorff for I.map phi. For a quotient class represented by r in R, surjectivity of residue composed with alpha supplies a coefficient a with alpha(a) congruent to r modulo m. The constant series C a maps to that quotient class, proving surjectivity of the quotient composite. Apply surjective_of_mk_map_comp_surjective to get surjectivity of phi. This is the source proof's direct 0315 argument; it does not use the 031D finite-module detour.
